title: DataAccessV1dot23
description: K-05 v1.23, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1531: T-1529's ruling card 2, ops/reviews/refusal-reply/rule-refusal.json; DL-1142, DL-1144): parkTurn parks a turn at once on a final refusal, or after its third crash, with K-01's passedOn line in its one row and Rosie's team's K-37 parked_turns row behind it (README item 84). It only adds to v1.22 (data-access.v1.22.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.22 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes but the two it restates, parkTurn.request (v1's form, or v1.23's parkTurn.lineRequest) and parkTurn.exchange (to refer to v1.23's request; the response and errors v1's, by reference), so every v1 to v1.22 exchange is a v1.23 exchange. Added: parkReason (a final refusal's labels: from, fault and ids, each a K-08 safeId), parkedLinePlan and parkedLineParts (the row's code-built plan and final parts, the passedOn line word for word), parkedRowNew (the one row, with its plan and final parts), parkTurn.lineRequest (the turn with tries 1 to 3, a reason before the third try, exactly one parkedRowNew, and its entries) and parkTurn.lineExchange (parkTurn.exchange narrowed to v1.23's request, the definition the v1.23 fixtures are listed under). No call, column, grant, index or migration is added: K-04 turns_tries_range already allows tries 1 to 3, K-37 v1's parked_turns is migrated (0014) and rosie_job holds SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on it. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

parkReason.title: ParkReason
parkReason.description: Why a turn is parked other than by crashes: a final refusal, as labels only (T-1529's ruling 2; README item 84, default 217): from, the part that refused it (such as walk, commit, companies, kinds, a read, or the Tool API base for notBuilt); fault, the refusal's own label (such as stepNotInBundle or secondCompany); ids, the steps, keys or rows at fault, as labels, or none. It is K-09 v1.13's turnRefused {from, fault, ids} (T-1529's ruling card 1), which the runtime passes across field for field. Each value is a K-08 v1 safeId (letters, digits and _ . : / # -, never a run that reads as a number), so no person's words, number or address and nothing of the refused part can stand in it (refuse-park-turn-sam-refused-reason-words), and nothing built from it can carry them. Which refusals are final is T-1529's ruling 1 and the runtime's to apply (README default 218), never checked here. New in v1.23.

from.description: The part that refused, as a label (K-09 v1.13 turnRefused.from).

fault.description: The refusal's own label, as the refusing part names it (K-09 v1.13 turnRefused.fault; for the walk, actions/src/commit/walk/errors.ts WalkFault).

ids.description: The steps, keys or rows at fault, as labels (step ids, the flow letter, a row id), in the refusing part's order; empty when it names none (K-09 v1.13 turnRefused.ids).

parkedLinePlan.title: ParkedLinePlan
parkedLinePlan.description: The plan the park's one row holds: K-03 v1 rowPlan, code-built as a fixed-line row's is (write-plan-alex-safety.json; v1.13's codeRowPlan), with no lines of its own, since its words are a fixed line code adds (arch 07 line 361): no text row it copies, formats text alone, no question (the line asks nothing, so no clock arms and no question is opened or moved), no page type and no thread. Its row and channel are the row's own, a code check as writePlan's (README item 84). New in v1.23.

parkedLineParts.title: ParkedLineParts
parkedLineParts.description: The final parts of the park's one row: K-03 v1 finalParts of one words send whose text is K-01's fixed line passedOn, word for word, as bundles/v2's manifest and K-01 v1's fixed-lines.json hold it, its two apostrophes the typographic one (arch 02 line 123; S13-29), fixedLines naming passedOn alone, and no calendar file, option, link, slot value or thread (README item 84, default 216). It is the standing default until Jay gives the park's own words (T-1529's ruling 2: no fixed line says 'nothing changed'; README open gap 103), sent only with the K-37 parked_turns row the same call writes, so the promise has Rosie's team's record behind it. So nothing the model wrote, no slot value and nothing of the refused part or of the turn's texts is in the row (refuse-park-turn-sam-refused-line-reworded). New in v1.23.

text.const: I’ve passed this on. Rosie’s team will reply within 1 business day.

parkedRowNew.title: ParkedRowNew
parkedRowNew.description: The park's one outbox row in v1.23's form (README item 84, default 219): v1's ten outboxRowNew fields, five by reference to v1's own definition of each (id, recipientHandleId, recipientPersonId, businessId, channel) and five pinned for the line (a quick reply, about no booking, asking no question, no email copy, decided on no versions, so limit 8 never finds it stale and clears its plan), and the code-built plan and final parts that put the passedOn line in it, written in the same transaction (parkedLinePlan, parkedLineParts). The row goes to the handle the turn's texts came from, on that handle's own way (runtime/src/turn/park.ts's defaults), and its id is the runtime's out-<turn id>-parked: code checks, as are the plan's and the final parts' row and channel matching the row's. New in v1.23.

bookingId.description: About no booking: the line names none (README default 219).

sendClass.description: A quick reply, a reply in the same turn (K-04 send class; Q-15), so limit 8 never holds it for text hours (README default 219).

openQuestionId.description: The line asks no question (README default 219).

copyOfRowId.description: No email copy: the row is its own (README default 219).

versionsRead.description: Decided on no versions, so limit 8 has none to compare and never moves the row to stale, which would clear its plan and leave an unworded parked row the claim passes (README default 183, default 219).

parkTurn.lineRequest.title: ParkTurnLineRequest
parkTurn.lineRequest.description: Park a turn in v1.23's form (T-1531; README item 84): at once on a final refusal (T-1529's ruling 2: no resend, no rerun; arch 11 line 576's park, applied sooner), or after a third crash before its commit, as v1's park (README item 12) plus the line (ruling card 7). The turn with its tries, 1 to 3; when it was parked; the refusal's labels (reason), required before the third try and allowed on it, left out for a crash; exactly one row, the passedOn line with its plan and final parts (parkedRowNew); and the event-log entries. The call also writes K-37 v1's parked_turns row for Rosie's team from the turn, the reason and parkedAt (README item 84, default 220). Nothing of the refused part travels: the reason is labels, the row's words are the fixed line. New in v1.23.

turn.description: The turn row, with its tries, 1 to 3 (v1's turn; K-04 turns_tries_range): a final refusal on any try, a crash on the third.

reason.description: The final refusal the turn is parked on (parkReason). Required before the third try, since only a final refusal parks a turn then; on the third, given for a final refusal and left out for a crash, which keeps v1's meaning (README default 218).

outboxRows.description: Exactly one row: the passedOn line, never an unworded row (README item 84).

parkTurn.request.title: ParkTurnRequest
parkTurn.request.description: Park a turn (README items 12 and 84): v1's form (v1.22's parkTurn.request, which is v1's: the turn with tries 3, at most one outbox row with no plan, its entries), which keeps working until the runtime's park moves (T-1529's ruling cards 6 and 7), or v1.23's (parkTurn.lineRequest: tries 1 to 3, a reason before the third try, exactly one row with the passedOn line). The two never overlap: a v1 row carries no plan, a v1.23 row always does. Changed in v1.23.

parkTurn.exchange.title: ParkTurnExchange
parkTurn.exchange.description: One parkTurn request with its outcome, restated in v1.23 to refer to v1.23's parkTurn.request. call and given are v1's own, by reference, and the response and errors v1's (parked, alreadyCommitted, transient): v1.23 adds no field or refusal to the answer, and a repeat answers its first park whatever its body or form (README default 223). So a request in v1's form is a v1.22 exchange. Changed in v1.23.

parkTurn.lineExchange.title: ParkTurnLineExchange
parkTurn.lineExchange.description: The exchange of a park in v1.23's form: parkTurn.exchange narrowed by allOf to parkTurn.lineRequest, as v1.22's commitTurn.rowLineExchange narrows the commit. The v1.23 fixtures are listed under this definition, so the loops that select parkTurn.exchange (db/repo/park.int.test.ts, whose first case pins park-turn.json as the one parkTurn.exchange) never meet them before the repo moves; it is the definition db/repo's answers to such a request are checked against (ruling card 4) and the runtime's park checks its requests by (cards 6 and 7). New in v1.23.
